public_rationale: OpenAI's later financing included Amazon, NVIDIA and Microsoft, so SoftBank was not its sole source of capital. However, the post already acknowledged other investors joining a SoftBank-arranged round. The stronger contextual claim is that SoftBank was indispensable. The later round still included SoftBank and does not establish that OpenAI could have financed itself without that support. Neither the survival funding requirement nor the necessity of SoftBank borrowing is demonstrated.
limitations: A literal sole-provider reading would give a different assessment of that component.
The evidence identifies actual financing arrangements, not the alternatives available without SoftBank.
Committed capital is not treated as cash already received.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: To survive, OpenAI must continue raising more money than any startup has ever raised before, and it can only do so from SoftBank, which in turn must take on debt.

statement.excerpt: To survive, OpenAI must continue raising more money than any startup has ever raised before, and they are only able to do so from SoftBank, which in turn must take on debt.

our_interpretation: This asserts necessary financing conditions for survival, rather than merely predicting that another funding round will occur.

The post elsewhere explicitly acknowledges a syndicate of other investors. In that context, dependence on SoftBank can mean dependence on its backing or arrangement of the round, not that every dollar must originate from SoftBank.
The ordinary test is whether OpenAI could obtain sufficient continuing finance without indispensable SoftBank support, and whether SoftBank could provide its necessary support without borrowing.
'To survive' describes the purpose of financing, not a conditional antecedent whose occurrence must first be established.
The startup funding comparison does not specify a single round, cumulative capital raised or a particular financing instrument.
criteria.support_condition: Financial records establish the amount of financing necessary for OpenAI's survival, show that it exceeded the relevant historical startup funding record, demonstrate that adequate alternatives to SoftBank were unavailable, and establish that SoftBank needed debt to supply the required support.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes an adequate financing path independent of indispensable SoftBank support, survival without the alleged record funding requirement, or sufficient SoftBank resources to provide the necessary support without borrowing.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI announced a closed round with $122 billion in committed capital and multiple major backers. This rejects literal sole-provider exclusivity, but SoftBank still participated and the announcement does not establish what financing was available without it.
